topics.topic: ArtifactPointer lifecycle when its project is deleted whole
questions: When the owner deletes an archived project whole, are its ArtifactPointer records deleted with it or retained, and if retained, through which product action can they still be read?
What happens to a project’s ArtifactPointer records when the owner deletes the project whole rather than anonymising it?
What happens to every ArtifactPointer naming a Project when the owner deletes that Project whole?

quotes: archived -> deleted whole     (owner, confirming; the record is gone, R0-60)

Durable, a record of its own naming its project (M01); kept after
anonymisation (R0-62).

Durable, a record of its own naming its project (M01); it goes when the
project is anonymised or deleted.

erase an archived project | owner, confirming | the project anonymised — its id, status and artifact pointers stay, its name, object and customer link go, `validate` answers `archived` — or deleted whole, `validate` answering `not_found`; the owner chooses (R0-60); either way it leaves every agent session's set and is active in none (R0-61)

list artifacts | owner; a trusted service; Kernel for the agent on a project its session is granted (R0-46) | every pointer of the project — published, superseded and withdrawn — each with its type, version and status; this is how history is read (R0-02) | unknown project refused as not found
judgement.divergence: One implementer deletes every ArtifactPointer with the deleted Project; another retains the separately durable pointer records as orphans, although normal artifact reads by project are refused because the project is not found. The owner notices the difference in retained Registry data and erasure behavior, and callers or services would notice if any later administrative, migration, audit, or recovery path exposes the retained records.
judgement.why: State 1 defines pointer persistence after anonymisation and room deletion with a deleted project, but leaves the pointer lifecycle for whole-project deletion unspecified.

topics.topic: AuditEntry identity and the role of its ordinal sequence number
questions: Is an AuditEntry’s ordinal sequence number an explicit exception to the UUID rule, or does the entry need a separate UUID identity while the sequence number serves only as ordering data?

topics.topic: Durable preservation of the last-issued audit sequence after entry erasure
questions: Which durable model or instance fact preserves the last-issued audit sequence after the owner erases the entry carrying the greatest sequence number, especially after all entries are erased?

topics.topic: Initial last-changed instant for a newly created Project or Customer
questions: What last-changed instant does a Project or Customer receive when its record is first created?

topics.topic: Revision and time invariants for Project and Customer records surviving erasure
questions: Do the revision and time invariants apply only before a Project is anonymised or a Customer erased, or must those surviving records retain revisions and times?
